instructions: Crack the 8 eggs into a bowl. Add the 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper and beat them with a fork until there are no streaks of white left. Thinly slice 3 of the green onions.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium low heat. Add the green onions and cook for about 1 minute, until they soften.

Pour in the eggs and leave them for about 20 seconds. Then push them slowly across the pan with a spatula so they gather into large, soft curds. After 2 to 3 minutes, while they still look a little glossy, transfer them to a plate. They finish cooking inside the tortillas. Wipe out the skillet.

Lay the 4 tortillas flat. Scatter 3/4 cup of the cheese over one half of each tortilla, dividing it evenly. Spoon the eggs over the cheese, then scatter the other 3/4 cup of cheese on top. Fold the bare half over and press it down flat.
Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add 2 of the quesadillas and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp.

Flip them and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes, until it's golden and the cheese has melted. If the tortilla browns before the cheese melts, turn the heat down a little. Transfer them to a cutting board.
Melt the last 1 tbsp of butter in the skillet and cook the other 2 quesadillas the same way.
Cut each quesadilla into 3 wedges. Serve with 1/2 cup of the salsa and 1/2 cup of the sour cream.
method_notes: All three fill a flour tortilla with eggs and melting cheese and crisp it in a skillet for a couple of minutes a side, folded in half. Natasha's Kitchen (the lead) cooks the eggs as a thin layer right onto the tortilla and adds sausage, bacon or ham, while Love and Lemons and A Couple Cooks scramble the eggs first, with scallions (Love and Lemons) or beans and pepper (A Couple Cooks). This follows the lead's 2 eggs and one large tortilla per person, but scrambles the eggs with green onions as the dish describes and leaves out the meat, with salsa and sour cream on the side as Love and Lemons serves them.
